title: Vellutata di Castagne Umbra
author: Marco Bellini
desc: A velvety Umbrian chestnut soup, chestnuts simmered with vegetables and blended completely smooth, finished with a swirl of cream and a scattering of crisp pancetta.
longDesc: Umbria's mountainous terrain has long supported chestnut cultivation, and this smooth, comforting soup showcases the nut's naturally sweet, earthy character in a form entirely different from Tuscany's dense castagnaccio cake.
ingredients: 60 ml (1/4 cup) extra virgin olive oil
steps: Warm the olive oil in a large pot and saute the onion, carrot, and celery until softened.
Add the chestnuts and stock, and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 20-25 minutes until the vegetables and chestnuts are very tender.
Blend the soup until completely smooth, using an immersion blender or transferring to a standing blender.
Return to the pot, stir in the cream, and gently reheat without boiling.
Meanwhile, if using, cook the pancetta in a small pan until crisp.
Season the soup to taste and serve hot, topped with crisp pancetta and fresh thyme.
chefTips: Pre-cooked, vacuum-packed chestnuts save considerable time over roasting and peeling your own.
Blend the soup thoroughly for the silkiest, most velvety texture.
The crisp pancetta topping provides a nice textural contrast to the smooth soup, though it can be omitted for a vegetarian version.
commonMistakes: Not blending thoroughly enough, leaving a grainy rather than silky-smooth texture.
Boiling the soup after adding the cream, which can cause it to separate.
Using low-quality chestnuts, which can taste bland or slightly bitter.
reheating: Reheat gently on the stovetop without boiling.
healthBenefits: Chestnuts provide fiber and complex carbohydrates, with less fat than most other nuts.
culturalNote: Vellutata di castagne reflects Umbria's mountainous chestnut-growing tradition, a comforting autumn soup found throughout the region's rural trattorie.
